methods: setting up linear equations from remainders
statement: The polynomial $p(x)=x^{3}+ax^{2}+bx+c$ leaves remainder $2$ when divided by $x-1$, remainder $-6$ when divided by $x+1$, and has a factor $x-2$. Find $a$, $b$ and $c$.
solution: By the remainder theorem, $p(1)=1+a+b+c=2$ so $a+b+c=1$. Also $p(-1)=-1+a-b+c=-6$ so $a-b+c=-5$. Since $x-2$ is a factor, $p(2)=8+4a+2b+c=0$ so $4a+2b+c=-8$. Subtracting the first two equations gives $2b=6$, hence $b=3$. Then $a+c=-2$ and $4a+c=-14$, so subtracting gives $3a=-12$, hence $a=-4$ and $c=2$. Thus $a=-4$, $b=3$, $c=2$.
hints: Write p(1), p(-1) and p(2) from the given conditions.
Subtract two of the equations to find b.
Solve the remaining two equations for a and c.
